name: Master Sourdough (Loaf + Pizza)
steps: Autolyse: mix flour and water until no dry flour remains; cover and rest 45 min (no salt yet).
Add the starter and salt; incorporate fully by pinching and folding.
Bulk ferment ~3 h with 4-5 sets of stretch and folds ~30 min apart, until stronger and risen 30-50% (watch the dough, not the clock; a warm kitchen is faster).
Divide into two roughly equal pieces.
Loaf half: shape a tight boule or batard, seam up in a floured bowl or banneton.
Proof the loaf at room temperature (~3.5 h) until it passes the poke test, or refrigerate overnight (12-24 h sweet spot).
Pizza half: shape a tight ball, place in a lightly oiled container and refrigerate at least 12-24 h.

Bake the loaf: preheat the oven to max (230-250°C) with a metal tray on the bottom rack. Score at ~30°, load, pour a cup of hot water into the tray, cover loosely with an upside-down metal bowl or roasting pan; bake 20 min.
Uncover and bake ~25 min more until deeply golden. Cool at least 1-2 h before cutting.
Pizza: ~1 h before, preheat your heaviest flat baking sheet upside down at max (250-280°C).
Stretch the chilled dough thin on a semolina-dusted surface or peel; top lightly and launch quickly.
Bake ~10 min on the hot pan until the bottom is charred and the cheese is bubbling.
notes: 70% hydration; use wet hands instead of extra flour. One batch = one ~600 g rustic loaf + one 30-35 cm pizza base (1 serving = half the dough, before toppings; a ~50 g slice of bread is ~125 kcal). Needs a live starter (see Sourdough Starter). Regular home oven only; Claude recommended a 10 mm+ pizza steel over a stone. Pitfalls: weigh everything in grams, do not cut the loaf hot, do not open the oven in the first 15-20 min, use drained mozzarella and light toppings, semolina under the pizza. timeMin counts the overnight cold ferment.

name: Sourdough Starter from Scratch

ingredients.item: whole rye or whole wheat flour
ingredients.note: per feed; not white flour in the first week
50 g per feed; room temperature, non-chlorinated (let tap water sit 1 h or use filtered)

steps: Day 1: mix 50 g flour + 50 g water in a clean wide-mouth jar; cover loosely (not sealed); keep at room temperature.
Day 2: ignore early bubbles; discard all but 50 g, add 50 g flour + 50 g water; stir, cover, wait 24 h.
Days 3-5: repeat the daily feed (discard to 50 g, add 50 g + 50 g). A sluggish starter with a sharp or acetone smell is normal; do not throw it out.
Days 5-10: keep feeding daily until it reliably doubles within 4-8 h and smells pleasantly tangy (a warm Bucharest August may be day 5-7).
Readiness: a spoonful floats in water; wait for 2-3 consecutive days of reliable doubling before the first bake.
Maintenance: keep a small 30-50 g mother in the fridge and feed it every 1-2 weeks; to bake, build it up over 1-2 feeds, pinch a bit back as the new mother and use the rest.
At each feed, wipe the jar walls above the starter level; move it to a freshly washed jar every 1-2 weeks.
notes: Not eaten on its own (macros not applicable). Mold (fuzzy, pink/black/orange/red) = toss everything and restart; dark liquid "hooch" means hunger, not mold. Mold causes: starving it young, an airtight lid, an unwiped film, a dirty jar, fridging too early. Discard is usable in pancakes, crackers and flatbread. Shortcut: ask a Bucharest bakery (Pain Plaisir, Casa del Pan) for a piece, or buy dehydrated live starter.
